object.title: Neumann-Lara's conjecture on NL-2-coflows of planar digraphs
object.statement:
A **loopless planar digraph** is a planar directed graph with no loops. An NL-$2$-coflow is a coflow whose associated pair satisfies the NL-coflow condition; equivalently, by the preceding characterization, its support contains a feedback arc set.

**Neumann-Lara's conjecture.** Every loopless planar digraph admits an NL-$2$-coflow.

Via planar duality, NL-coflows correspond to NL-flows in the dual digraph. The conjecture is the coflow formulation of Neumann-Lara's conjecture concerning acyclic vertex colorings of planar digraphs; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Barbara Altenbokum, Winfried Hochstättler and Johanna Wiehe, “The NL-flow polynomial”, arXiv:1901.01871 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01871

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

object.title: Period-denominator equality for two-move rider chess-piece configurations
object.statement:
Let $u_\mathbb{P}(q;n)$ be the counting quasipolynomial for nonattacking configurations of $q$ copies of a two-move rider $\mathbb{P}$ on the dilated unit board, and let $D([0,1]^{2q},\mathcal{A}_\mathbb{P}^q)$ be the denominator of the associated inside-out polytope. The period of $u_\mathbb{P}(q;n)$ is the shortest length of its cyclic sequence of constituent polynomials. **Period-denominator equality conjecture.** The period of the counting quasipolynomial $u_\mathbb{P}(q;n)$ equals the denominator

$$
D([0,1]^{2q},\mathcal{A}_\mathbb{P}^q).
$$

The period always divides the denominator by Ehrhart theory, but equality is generally surprising because periods can be smaller than denominators; this conjecture asserts equality for these chess-piece counting quasipolynomials.
object.source_name: Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Arvind V. Mahankali, “A billiards-like dynamical system for attacking chess pieces”, arXiv:1901.01917 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01917

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

object.title: The Edelman–Greene coefficient bound
object.statement:
Let $w$ be a permutation and let $a_{w,\lambda}$ denote the corresponding Edelman–Greene coefficient for a partition $\lambda$, with $f^{\lambda}$ the number of standard Young tableaux of shape $\lambda$. **Edelman–Greene coefficient bound.** One has

$$
a_{w,\lambda}\leq f^{\lambda}.
$$

This bound was stated in the paper as a conjecture and has since been proved by G. Orelowitz in private communication.
object.source_name: Cara Monical, Benjamin Pankow and Alexander Yong, “Reduced word enumeration, complexity, and randomization”, arXiv:1901.03247 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.03247

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2019). “The following conjecture has been proved by G. Orelowitz (private communication):”

object.title: Serbanuta's conjecture on attainable M-ambiguity sequences
object.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be an ordered alphabet. For words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$ and a letter $a\in\Sigma$, a word is **$M$-unambiguous** if it is not $M$-equivalent to any distinct word, where $M$-equivalence means having the same Parikh matrix. **Serbanuta's conjecture.** If $uaav$ is $M$-unambiguous, then $uav$ is $M$-unambiguous. Equivalently, if $uav$ is $M$-ambiguous, then $uaav$ is also $M$-ambiguous. This conjecture concerns the possible patterns of $M$-ambiguity under insertion of a repeated letter and was proposed as an open problem by Serbanuta; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Wen Chean Teh and Ghajendran Poovanandran, “M-Ambiguity Sequences for Parikh Matrices and Their Periodicity Revisited”, arXiv:1901.03937 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.03937

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

object.title: Nonnegativity conjecture for the cd-index of regular CW spheres
object.statement: A regular CW sphere is a regular CW complex whose underlying space is a sphere, and its $cd$-index is the polynomial $\Phi_P(c,d)$ encoding its flag $f$-vector, with $c$ of degree $1$ and $d$ of degree $2$. **Nonnegativity conjecture.** The coefficients in the $cd$-index of every regular CW sphere are nonnegative. This extends the nonnegativity known for convex polytopes to all regular CW spheres; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
object.source_name: Margaret M. Bayer, “The cd-Index: A Survey”, arXiv:1901.04939 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.04939

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

object.title: Acyclicity conjecture for the mutation graph of positive braids
object.statement: A positive braid word is a word in the braid generators with only positive exponents, and its mutation graph has vertices given by equivalence classes of Demazure weaves and edges corresponding to mutations. Orient every mutation in the direction $(ss)s\to s(ss)$. **Mutation-graph acyclicity conjecture.** For any positive braid $\beta$, this orientation descends to the mutation graph of $\beta$, and the resulting oriented graph has no oriented cycles. This predicts a well-defined acyclic orientation on the mutation graph, supporting its interpretation as an exchange graph for a cluster algebra.
object.source_name: Roger Casals, Eugene Gorsky, Mikhail Gorsky and José Simental, “Algebraic Weaves and Braid Varieties”, arXiv:2012.06931 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.06931

object.title: Conjecture on the adjacency-matrix inequality for graph normalization
object.statement:
Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a connected simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $x\in{\mathbb{R}^{+*}}^n$. Define

$$
y=x\oslash(A+I)x.
$$

**Graph-normalization adjacency inequality conjecture.** The inequality

$$
y^t(A+I)y\leq\lVert y\rVert_1
$$

holds. This is the paper's main conjecture underlying its proposed proof of general convergence: if true, it implies that the $L_1$ norm of the weights increases under normalization and converges, although convergence of the norm alone does not establish convergence of the weight vector.
object.source_name: Laurent Guigues, “Concerning Iterative Graph Normalization and Maximum Weight Independent Sets”, arXiv:2012.07764 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

object.title: Singleton-optimizer stability conjecture
object.statement: Let $OPT$ be the set of optimal vectors for the graph-density optimization problem under consideration, and let a problem be **stable** when every near-optimal graph is close to an optimal construction. **Singleton-optimizer stability conjecture.** If $OPT$ consists of a single point, then the problem is necessarily stable. The claim is posed as an open question in the paper; its general validity is not established there.
object.source_name: Hong Liu, Oleg Pikhurko, Maryam Sharifzadeh and Katherine Staden, “Stability from graph symmetrisation arguments with applications to inducibility”, arXiv:2012.10731 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.10731

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

object.title: Positive-isolated-part conjecture for clique-density optimizers
object.statement:
For $2\leq i\leq k$, let $a_i$ be coefficients and define 
$$
\lambda(G):=\sum_{i=2}^k a_i p(K_i,G),
$$
 where $p(K_i,G)$ is the induced density of $K_i$. Let $OPT$ denote the set of optimal vectors, and write $x_0$ for the coordinate corresponding to the isolated part. **Positive-isolated-part conjecture.** If $OPT$ contains $\mathbold{x}$ with $x_0>0$, then necessarily $x_0=1$. The paper presents this as an open question alongside other structural questions about optimal vectors; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
object.source_name: Hong Liu, Oleg Pikhurko, Maryam Sharifzadeh and Katherine Staden, “Stability from graph symmetrisation arguments with applications to inducibility”, arXiv:2012.10731 (2023).

object.title: The awesome conjecture for coefficients of the logarithmic expansion
object.statement:
Let $z_i\geq2$ be positive integers, and define

$$
F=\sum_{s\geq0}\frac{a_s(r,j)}{n^s}+\sum_i c_i j(j-1)\cdots(j-z_i+1)\frac{1}{n^{z_i}r^{z_i}}\sum_{s\geq0}\frac{a_s(r,j-z_i)}{n^s}.
$$

For coefficient extraction, $[j^k n^{-h}]$ denotes the coefficient of $j^k n^{-h}$.

**The awesome conjecture.**

$$
[j^k n^{-h}]\,\ln(F)=0,\qquad k\geq h+2,
$$

and

$$
[j^{h+1}n^{-h}]\,\ln(F)=\frac{1}{(h+1)h}\left(\frac{1}{r^h}-2\right).
$$

The source identifies this as an earlier conjecture and contrasts it with a weaker theorem proved in the paper. Its general status is not resolved by the supplied text.
object.source_name: Paul Federbush, “A PROOF of Weak Graph Positivity, for a Large Range of the Parameters”, arXiv:2012.10927 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.10927

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

object.title: Both-shifts versus one-direction shift-pattern conjecture
object.statement: Let $G_{m,n}$ denote the grid under discussion, and let $m,n,k,z\in\mathbb{N}^+$. A $k$-coloring has a shift pattern in both directions on $z$-subgrids, or in only one direction on $z$-subgrids, according to the stipulated shift-pattern condition. **Both-shifts versus one-direction conjecture.** For $m,n,k,z\in\mathbb{N}^+$, if a $k$-coloring of $G_{m,n}$ with shift pattern in both directions on $z$-subgrids exists, then a $k$-coloring of $G_{m,n}$ with shift pattern in only one direction on $z$-subgrids exists. This is motivated by the observed implication in the reported table, but the source presents it as an open problem and explains that the necessary color-distribution constraints for both shifts are substantially more difficult to analyze.
object.source_name: Zhenjun Liu, Leroy Chew and Marijn Heule, “Avoiding Monochromatic Rectangles Using Shift Patterns”, arXiv:2012.12582 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12582

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

object.title: The Shapley value is in the core of the energy game
object.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, with the energy game assigning each coalition its graph energy and with $\boldsymbol{\varphi}$ denoting the Shapley value. **Energy-game core conjecture.** For the energy game, the Shapley value is in the core. This conjecture asks whether the Shapley allocation satisfies all coalition inequalities for graph energy; the source gives an example showing that the energy value itself need not coincide with the Shapley value, but provides no resolution of the core-membership question.
object.source_name: Gerardo Arizmendi and Octavio Arizmendi, “The graph energy game”, arXiv:2012.14114 (2021).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.14114

object.title: Rowvacuation homomesy for the type B piecewise-linear statistic
object.statement:
Let $\mathsf{B}^n$ be the type B quotient poset, let $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{PL}}_{\kappa}(\mathsf{B}^n)$ denote its $kappa$-normalized piecewise-linear labelings, and define

$$
h^{\mathrm{PL}}_*(\pi) \coloneqq \sum_{\substack{p\in \mathsf{A}^{2n-1},\\ \operatorname{Flip}(p)=p}} \pi(\langle \operatorname{Flip}\rangle p).
$$

**The type B piecewise-linear homomesy conjecture.** The statistic $h^{\mathrm{PL}}_*\colon \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{PL}}_{\kappa}(\mathsf{B}^n)\to \mathbb{R}$ is $\kappa$-mesic for $\operatorname{Rvac}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\mathrm{PL}}$.
This extends the previously established rowvacuation homomesies for the statistics $h^{\mathrm{PL}}_i$; the embedding argument does not establish this additional statistic, so its asserted homomesy remains open.
object.source_name: Sam Hopkins and Michael Joseph, “The birational Lalanne-Kreweras involution”, arXiv:2012.15795 (2021).
object.references:

object.title: Archer et al.'s quasi-Stirling descent conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}=\{1^2,2^2,\ldots,n^2\}$, and let $\overline{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathcal{M}}$ denote the set of quasi-Stirling permutations of $\mathcal{M}$. For a permutation $\pi=\pi_1\pi_2\ldots\pi_{2n}$, define

$$
des(\pi)=|\{i\mid \pi_i>\pi_{i+1},\ 1\leq i\leq 2n-1\}|+1.
$$

**Archer et al.'s conjecture.** The number of $\pi\in\overline{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathcal{M}}$ with $des(\pi)=n$ is equal to

$$
(n+1)^{n-1}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the descent enumerator of quasi-Stirling permutations on the multiset in which every element occurs twice. It refines the known enumeration $|\overline{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathcal{M}}|=n!C_n$, where $C_n$ is the $n$th Catalan number; the supplied text gives no evidence that the descent-count assertion has been resolved.
object.source_name: Sherry H. F. Yan and Xue Zhu, “Quasi-Stirling Polynomials on Multisets”, arXiv:2106.04347 (2021).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2002.00985](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00985).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.04347

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

object.title: Ivanov's metaconjecture on automorphisms of rich surface objects
object.statement: Let $S$ be a surface, and let an object be naturally associated to $S$ and have sufficiently rich structure. **Ivanov's metaconjecture.** Every such object has the extended mapping class group ${\operatorname{Map}^\pm}(S)$ as its group of automorphisms. This metaconjecture describes a pattern in which sufficiently rich objects associated to finite-type surfaces are characterized by the action of the extended mapping class group; the paper explains that it does not extend to simultaneous flip graphs of infinite-type surfaces.
object.source_name: Assaf Bar-Natan, Advay Goel, Brendan Halstead, Paul Hamrick, Sumedh Shenoy and Rishi Verma, “Big Flip Graphs and Their Automorphism Groups”, arXiv:2201.11272 (2022).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2010.13169](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.13169).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11272

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: Unfriendly Partition Conjecture for countably infinite graphs
object.statement: A **majority $2$-vertex-coloring** of a graph is a coloring of its vertices with two colors such that, at every vertex, the number of neighbors having the same color is at most the number having the other color. **Unfriendly Partition Conjecture.** Every countably infinite graph admits a majority $2$-vertex-coloring. This is the countably infinite restriction of the broader Cowan–Emerson conjecture. Every infinite graph admits a majority $3$-vertex-coloring, but whether every countably infinite graph admits a majority $2$-vertex-coloring remains open.
object.source_name: Rafał Kalinowski, Monika Pilśniak and Marcin Stawiski, “List majority edge-colorings of graphs”, arXiv:2312.00922 (2023).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2003.02883](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02883).

object.title: Foley–Hoàng–Merkel's twinning conjecture for $(3+1)$-free posets
object.statement:
Let $P$ be a $(3+1)$-free poset, let $v\in P$, and let $P_v$ be the poset obtained by adding an element $v'$ that is incomparable to $w$ if and only if either $w=v$ or $w$ is incomparable to $v$. Let $\operatorname{Inc}(P)$ denote the incomparability graph of $P$.

**Foley–Hoàng–Merkel's twinning conjecture.** If $P$ is $(3+1)$-free and $X_{\operatorname{Inc}(P)}(\mathbf{x})$ is $e$-positive, then $X_{\operatorname{Inc}(P_v)}(\mathbf{x})$ is $e$-positive for any $v\in P$.

This is a weakened version of the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture, motivated by the fact that twinning preserves the property of being $(3+1)$-free. The source does not state that this conjecture has been resolved.
object.source_name: Esther Banaian, Kyle Celano, Megan Chang-Lee, Laura Colmenarejo, Owen Goff, Jamie Kimble, Lauren Kimpel, John Lentfer, Jinting Liang and Sheila Sundaram, “The e-positivity of the chromatic symmetric function for twinned paths and cycles”, arXiv:2405.17649 (2024).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2010.14312](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14312).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17649

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2024). “A counterexample to this conjecture was given by Li, Li, Wang, and Yang (2021).”

object.title: Spiro's bipartite quasikernel improvement conjecture
object.statement:
Let $D$ be a source-free bipartite digraph, meaning that every vertex has a nonempty set of external in-neighbors. A **quasikernel** of $D$ is an independent set $Q\subseteq V(D)$ such that every vertex $v\in V(D)$ satisfies $\operatorname{dist}_D(Q,v)\le 2$. **Spiro's bipartite quasikernel improvement conjecture.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, if $D$ has no directed $2$-cycle and no directed $4$-cycle, then $D$ has a quasikernel $Q$ with

$$
|Q|\le \left(\frac12-\varepsilon\right)|V(D)|.
$$

Spiro proved a strict improvement over the half bound for the relevant bipartite digraphs apart from the excluded cycle cases. The conjecture asks whether the improvement can be made uniform by a fixed positive $\varepsilon$; it remains open.
object.source_name: Zejun Huang and Chenxi Yang, “Three Results on Generalized Quasikernels in Digraphs”, arXiv:2607.09031 (2026).
object.references:
**8 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2606.16571](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16571), [arXiv:2606.16971](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16971), [arXiv:2406.04887](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04887), [arXiv:2404.07305](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07305), [arXiv:2312.15519](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15519), [arXiv:2110.00789](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00789), [arXiv:2001.04003](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04003).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09031

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

object.title: The shrubdepth characterization by paths
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a class of graphs, let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the class of paths, and let $\sqsupseteq_\mathrm{FO}$ denote the first-order transduction quasiorder. A graph class has **bounded shrubdepth** when it is first-order interpretable in some fixed finite-height rooted tree class. **The shrubdepth characterization by paths.** A class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded shrubdepth if and only if

$$
\mathcal{C}\not\sqsupseteq_\mathrm{FO}\mathcal{P}.
$$

This conjecture characterizes bounded shrubdepth by excluding the class of paths as a first-order transduction target. The surrounding discussion presents it as one of the difficult structural questions about the first-order transduction quasiorder; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
object.source_name: Jaroslav Nesetril, Patrice Ossona de Mendez and Sebastian Siebertz, “Structural properties of the first-order transduction quasiorder”, arXiv:2010.02607 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.02607

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2020). “It is still open whether the MSO transduction quasi-order is as shown above , though the initial fragment $\Ee\cover_\MSO \Tt_1\cover_\MSO\Tt_2\cover_\MSO\ldots\cover_\MSO\Tt_n$ has been proved to be as stated in .”

object.title: Kim's Italian domination conjecture for Cartesian products of directed cycles
object.statement:
Let $C_n$ denote the directed cycle of order $n$, and let $b3_I(D)$ be the Italian domination number of a digraph $D$. For an odd integer $n$, **Kim's conjecture.**

$$
\gamma_I(C_4 \Box C_n) = 2n + 2.
$$

This conjecture concerns Italian domination in the Cartesian product of a directed $4$-cycle and an odd directed cycle. The source states the conjecture but provides no resolution, so its status remains open.
object.source_name: Christopher M. van Bommel, “Italian Domination of Cartesian Products of Directed Cycles”, arXiv:2011.01078 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.01078

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).
